title: Outline GKE POC memory
purpose: Trace the Outline MVP/POC deployment attempt on GKE so future work can continue without relying on chat history.

repositoryRules.secretsPolicy: Do not store OAuth client secrets, API keys, database passwords, Redis passwords, SECRET_KEY, or UTILS_SECRET in this file.

plannedTencentProduction.scope: Formal Outline production service. The current GKE deployment remains a demo/POC only. Tencent Cloud pre-production and production start from zero; do not migrate any demo documents, attachments, users, permissions, API keys, or history.

locationAndAccess.productionEndpoint: A stable HTTPS domain is required. Public IP plus port is not an acceptable production access path.
locationAndAccess.icpRequirement: Complete ICP filing before opening public access. Tencent Cloud requires a domain for its filing workflow and does not support IP-only filing. Complete public-security filing within the required period after launch.
domainTasks: Allocate a company-owned domain such as kb.<company-domain> for Outline.
Use the same HTTPS origin as Outline URL, email magic-link origin, and OIDC callback origin.
Obtain a certificate and configure HTTPS on CLB before authentication validation.
Use a separate SES sender subdomain such as notify.<company-domain>.

capacityTarget.performanceValidationTarget: At least 150 concurrent sessions in pre-production, combining browsing, editing, same-document collaboration, and agent API writes.

recommendedDeployment.platform: Dedicated production TKE cluster spanning two or three availability zones.
recommendedDeployment.network: Dedicated VPC, private subnets for TKE, PostgreSQL, Redis, and COS access; public exposure only through HTTPS CLB, with commercial WAF a separate security and budget decision.

nodePool.minimum: Three on-demand 4 vCPU / 8 GiB nodes distributed across availability zones.
nodePool.autoscaling: Minimum 3, maximum 6 nodes. Do not use spot instances for the baseline capacity.

outlineServices: Web/API: minimum 3 replicas, HPA to 6, request 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, limit 2 vCPU / 4 GiB.
Collaboration: minimum 2 replicas, HPA to 4, request 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, limit 2 vCPU / 4 GiB.
Worker: minimum 2 replicas, HPA to 3, request 0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB.
outlineRuntimeRequirements: Run web, collaboration, worker, and cron as separate deployments instead of retaining the POC all-in-one deployment.
Set REDIS_COLLABORATION_URL to managed Redis before horizontally scaling collaboration.
Use WEB_CONCURRENCY=1 inside each Kubernetes container and scale with Pods; explicitly cap total database connection pools across all services.
Use an immutable Outline image tag and digest in Tencent Container Registry; never deploy latest tags.

managedDependencies.postgresql: TencentDB for PostgreSQL in dual-node high-availability mode, initial target 4 vCPU / 16 GiB with 200 GiB storage, private access, automatic growth alerting, daily full backups, and at least 30 days of log backups for point-in-time recovery.
managedDependencies.redis: TencentDB for Redis standard architecture, initial target 4 GiB with at least one replica, private access, automatic backup, and capacity alerts.
managedDependencies.objectStorage: Two private COS buckets: one for Outline attachments and one for backup exports. Enable versioning, encryption, lifecycle rules, and cross-bucket replication for the recovery bucket.
managedDependencies.mail: Tencent Cloud SES through a business-verified account with SMTP permissions, a verified sender subdomain, SPF/DKIM, and alerting for delivery failures and bounces. New personal-verified accounts cannot rely on SES SMTP after 2026-03-02.
managedDependencies.secrets: Tencent Cloud SSM plus TKE ExternalSecrets. Do not store database credentials, Redis credentials, SMTP credentials, SECRET_KEY, or UTILS_SECRET in source control or Helm values.
managedDependencies.delivery: Tencent Container Registry, Infrastructure as Code, and a separate pre-production environment before production changes.

authenticationPolicy.primary: Email OTP or magic link through SES after HTTPS and a stable domain are available.
authenticationPolicy.futureUnifiedEntry: Reserve standard OIDC issuer, client credentials, callback URL, and email-mapping configuration boundaries without enabling a provider in the first release. The future provider may be a Feilian-like corporate IdP, DingTalk, or Feishu; prefer federation through one IdP rather than Outline-specific changes per source.
authenticationPolicy.onboarding: Require invitations for new users. Do not enable unrestricted public registration for the internal knowledge base.
authenticationPolicy.agentIdentity: Issue personal API keys to users and separate bot identities to automated agents; use minimum scopes, rotation, revocation, and audit review.

requiredArtifacts: PostgreSQL backups and point-in-time recovery logs.
COS attachment objects and historical versions.
Infrastructure and application manifests held in version control.
Recoverable copies of stable application secrets held in SSM.
backupAndRecovery.exercise: Run a monthly isolated restore rehearsal: restore database and attachments, inject production secrets, then verify sign-in, document counts, attachments, permissions, API access, and collaboration.

monitoringAndAlerts.platform: TKE monitoring plus Tencent Cloud Prometheus/Grafana, TencentDB metrics, CLB/WAF logs, external HTTPS synthetic monitoring, and Sentry for application errors.
criticalAlerts: Public HTTPS or Outline health check unavailable.
No ready Web/API or collaboration Pods.
PostgreSQL availability, storage, connections, or backup failure.
Redis availability, memory, or replication failure.
Unexpected error rate, latency, queue backlog, or authentication failures.

releaseAndUpgradePolicy.outline: Test every image and database migration against a production-like pre-production clone. Take verified backups before migration and keep an approved rollback or restore path.
releaseAndUpgradePolicy.postgresql: Treat a major version upgrade as protected maintenance, not zero downtime: rehearse against a clone, schedule a read-only window, validate application behavior, and retain pre-upgrade backups.
testScenarios: Email invitation, login, logout, disabled-user, delivery-failure, and bounce checks; verify that the OIDC configuration/callback boundary remains ready without enabling a provider.
Role, collection, document, and API-key authorization boundaries.
Document editing, same-document collaboration, search, import/export, and COS attachments.
API and MCP read/write attribution with user and bot identities.
Pod restart, Redis disruption, database failover, attachment failure, and full restore rehearsal.
Load test at 1.5 times the expected peak concurrency.

gkeToProductionMigration.details: Create clean Tencent Cloud pre-production and production databases, Redis instances, COS buckets, SSM secret namespaces, administrator workspace, users, invitations, and API keys. GKE only supplies POC findings and test cases.

exclusions: Corporate IdP, DingTalk, Feishu, or other third-party licensing.
Cross-region disaster recovery, SMS, external security assessment, and unexpected large attachment egress.

apiKeyAttributionFindings.summary: Outline API keys are personal keys. API authentication resolves the request user from apiKey.userId; document updates then set document.lastModifiedById to that user id and present it to clients as updatedBy.
apiKeyAttributionFindings.currentMvpImplication: If agents use only an admin-owned API key, UI metadata, revisions, and document history will attribute document changes to that admin user, not to the colleague who requested the agent action.
builtInTraceFields: documents.updatedBy / documents.lastModifiedById show the attributed user.
revisions.userId and revision collaborators show the attributed editor(s).
events.actorId, events.authType, events.ip, and events.changes capture mutation context.
apiKeyAttributionFindings.limitation: Built-in events record authType=api and actorId, but do not persist the specific apiKey id used for each request. Multiple keys owned by the same user are not distinguishable from document history alone.

keyFindings: For domestic or Alibaba Cloud style deployment, keep Outline containerized but move durability concerns to managed PostgreSQL, Redis/Tair, and OSS/S3-compatible object storage when possible.
Keep SECRET_KEY and UTILS_SECRET stable across deployments; losing or regenerating them can invalidate tokens and encrypted data.
Real email login and document/invite notifications require a real outbound SMTP service. Mailpit is only an MVP stub.
Outline currently has generic OIDC support but no native DingTalk or Feishu auth provider in this repository.
The lowest-risk enterprise login path is an OIDC bridge such as IDaaS/Keycloak/Authing; direct DingTalk or Feishu OAuth requires a custom Outline auth plugin.
Switching login to OIDC/DingTalk/Feishu does not remove the need for SMTP, because notification emails are sent by Outline through SMTP.
recommendedSequence: Add a real domain and HTTPS.
Replace Mailpit with a real SMTP provider and verify magic-link login plus notification emails.
Design the domestic durable deployment around PostgreSQL backup/restore and attachment storage migration.
Run an OIDC/IDaaS POC and confirm user identity fields, API-key attribution, and email notifications.
Only then evaluate whether native DingTalk or Feishu auth plugins are worth building.
